correctness.rationale: The support function is ||y||_2+s|y1|, so the polar has exact disk sections on 0<=x<=1/(1+s). Fubini evaluates polar volume as 2pi(s+2)/(3(1+s)^2), while the original volume is 2pi(2+3s)/3. The polynomial identity 4(1+s)^2-(2+3s)(2+s)=s^2 gives the exact deficit for all s>=0. Differentiation gives -8pi^2 s/[9(1+s)^3]. The cylinder limit follows by uniform support convergence. A standard-library checker independently passed exact rational checks and numerical spherical-polar integration checks.

value.rationale: The family is the canonical Euclidean ball thickened by a segment; volume product is a key affine invariant with nontrivial global stability literature. The result gives a sharp dimension-three family-wide stability curve, an exact quadratic coefficient for the axial deformation, and a sharp nonellipsoidal limiting benchmark. These precise constants and the curve are not supplied by the global upper or lower inequalities. Scope is one natural family, not a universal theorem.
